course_name_original: Técnicas de Medida y Tratamiento de Datos en Ingeniería Energética
course_name_en: Measurement Techniques and Data Processing in Energy Engineering
prerequisites: Basic knowledge and competencies from degree programs or equivalent that have received training corresponding to basic subjects in Physics and Mathematics, as well as notions of Thermodynamics, Heat Transfer, and Fluid Mechanics.
Basic knowledge of computer programs for calculations and representation of results, such as Microsoft Excel or Matlab.

learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context.

That students know how to apply the acquired knowledge and their problem-solving ability in new or unfamiliar environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their area of study.

That students are able to integrate knowledge and face the complexity of formulating judgments from information that, being incomplete or limited, includes reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
That students know how to communicate their conclusions and the ultimate knowledge and reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
That students possess learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a way that will largely be self-directed or autonomous.

Have adequate knowledge of the scientific and technological aspects of: mathematical, analytical and numerical methods in engineering, electrical engineering, energy engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, continuum mechanics, industrial electronics, automation, manufacturing, materials, quantitative management methods, industrial informatics, urban planning and infrastructures.
Project, calculate and design products, processes, installations and plants.
Carry out research, development and innovation in products, processes and methods.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Engineer.
Knowledge and skills for the design and analysis of thermal machines and engines, hydraulic machines and industrial heating and cooling installations.
Knowledge and capacities that allow understanding, analyzing, exploiting and managing the different energy sources.

Knowledge and capacities for projecting and designing electrical and fluid installations, lighting, air conditioning and ventilation, energy saving and efficiency, acoustics, communications, home automation and intelligent buildings, and security installations.
Knowledge and capacities for carrying out verification and control of installations, processes and products.
Knowledge and capacities for carrying out certifications, audits, verifications, tests and reports.
Know the physical-mathematical models that can be posed in mass, momentum and energy transfer processes and the simplifications to be made to solve the governing equations.
Identify, analyze and evaluate the variables involved in a thermal or fluid process.
Choose the most convenient sensors and measurement equipment for the real study of a fluid-mechanical and/or thermal phenomenon.
Analyze the errors and uncertainties produced in a measurement.
Design experiments through which data for a fluid-mechanical and/or thermal phenomenon can be obtained.
Employ computer tools for data acquisition and processing.

syllabus_topics: Experiments, variables and measurements in Energy Engineering
Sensors used in the measurement of variables in thermal or fluid processes
Signal acquisition, processing and analysis systems in temporal and frequency domains.
teaching_methods: Virtual Campus activities (reading theoretical foundations, solving questionnaires, participating in debate forums, viewing materials)
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as (0.4 x Active Participation) + (0.3 x Practical Work P1) + (0.3 x Practical Work P2). For the extraordinary call, the final grade is calculated as (0.6 x Theoretical Exam T1) + (0.2 x Practical Work P1) + (0.2 x Practical Work P2), where P1 and P2 notes are retained from continuous assessment. For differentiated assessment, the final grade is calculated as (0.6 x Theoretical Exam T1) + (0.4 x Practical Work P1). No minimum grade is required for any individual element in any call.
